general_information.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_information.Description: In this course, students are introduced to a fundamental understanding of Public Relations basics, strategic planning, and media relations. Students will learn in-depth about types of content, including written, visual, multimedia, interactive, and social media content. Students also comprehend the importance of storytelling, content development, and management for PR. Especially, students are instructed in leveraging AI tools to enhance the creative process. Additionally, students are provided with an understanding of strategies of content so that they can flexibly apply them in different PR scenarios. They will learn how to use metrics to evaluate PR campaigns and craft comprehensive communication strategies. After the course, students will be able to effectively and ethically plan, execute, and measure PR campaigns.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance

description: In this course, students are introduced to a fundamental understanding of Public Relations basics, strategic planning, and media relations. Students will learn in-depth about types of content, including written, visual, multimedia, interactive, and social media content. Students also comprehend the importance of storytelling, content development, and management for PR. Especially, students are instructed in leveraging AI tools to enhance the creative process. Additionally, students are provided with an understanding of strategies of content so that they can flexibly apply them in different PR scenarios. They will learn how to use metrics to evaluate PR campaigns and craft comprehensive communication strategies. After the course, students will be able to effectively and ethically plan, execute, and measure PR campaigns.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Comprehend the role and importance of PR in organizations, the basics of PR strategy, and media relations.
Comprehend types of PR content, including written, visual, multimedia, interactive, and social media content, as well as the role of storytelling in producing PR content.
Produce, manage, and edit various types of PR content effectively in different scenarios, particularly by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools throughout the process.
Select and execute rational strategies for PR content effectively in different scenarios.
Plan, execute, and measure the effectiveness of PR campaigns effectively, and assemble overview reports after campaigns.
Demonstrate a professional and positive attitude, and be accountable, ethical when professionally applying PR strategies and execution in real life.

assessments.Note: Participation grade will be given based on students' attendance, students' attitude, preparation, contribution of discussions

assessments.Question Type: In group of 3-5, develop a PR campaign which may include: - SMART Objectives, Campaign Channels, Campaign Mediums, Media List, Content, Pitch, Target audience, stakeholders.Then generate pieces of content for your campaign such as media posts, blog, or press release. Students are allowed to use AI to generate types of content.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Possess the necessary skills and abilities to develop and implement effective public relations plans for a wide range of entertainment activities.
assessments.Grading Guide: Suggested criteria: Campaign (80%) SMART Objectives (20%) Campaign Channels (10%) Campaign Mediums (10%) Media List (5%) Content Plan (5%) Pitch (5%) Target audience (5%) Content pieces (10%) - AI usage (10%) Oral presentations (20%) - Content (5%) - Quality of presentation slides and/or any other multimedia production if it has (5%) - Verbal and non-verbal delivery (5%) - Critical and logical responses to questions raised by examiners (5%)
assessments.Note: According to the predetermined LOs, lecturers have the flexibility to choose assignment forms. Each assignment has a six-day due date, which commences when the lecture provides detailed instructions.

assessments.Question Type: Report: Students are required to create an experience map for a brand that they love. This assignment helps students to identify the influence of content and touchpoint in different stages of customer experience.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Possess the necessary skills and abilities to develop and implement effective public relations plans for a wide range of entertainment activities.
assessments.Grading Guide: suggested criteria: Introduction & Brand Overview (10%) Customer Persona (10%) Experience Map structure (15%) Touchpoints Identification (10%) Content types (10%) Customer Thoughts, Feelings, Actions (10%) Brand Response (10%) Analysis of Effectiveness (15%) References & Research (5%) Presentation & Creativity (5%)
assessments.Note: According to the predetermined LOs, lecturers have the flexibility to choose assignment forms. Each assignment has a six-day due date, which commences when the lecture provides detailed instructions.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: A comprehensive understanding of the relationship between entertainment and communication from both theoretical and practical approaches
